dispatched_note: 303rd BG Mission 78 report table: 1st CBW = 91BG (11) high, 381BG (17) low (wing led by Col. Milton) - single source, possibly planned figure. No 381st loading list or sortie list for 14 Oct 1943 was found online. Squadron war diaries (381st BGMA transcriptions) give: 532nd - six ships took off (Beckman, Clore, Wood, Moore, Hutchens, Baltrusaitis [early return, oxygen]) plus a mention of Lt Miller returning early; 533rd - six 533rd aircraft took part (pilots Cahow, Crozier named; four flown by other squadrons' crews); 534th - five airborne at 1035 (Ohl, Niederriter, Schomburg, Miller [abort], Yorba [MIA]); 535th - Chapman, Baer, Hopp, Crosson, Ridley. These overlap (533rd aircraft flown by other squadrons' crews), so the total is roughly 17-22 and not established. 242nd Medical Detachment diary: "three abortions in our group"; take-off 1035, return 1735. 381st missions list: group mission #39.
lost_note: One aircraft lost: 42-29803 (Yorba), MACR 1037 (381st casualty list, 381st MACR list, 535th BS diary "losing only one aircraft"). The 1st CBW diary says the wing (91st + 381st) lost three. b17flyingfortress.de lists 42-29784, 42-29867 and 42-29988 under the 381st as well, but its unit column covers each aircraft's whole service: 42-29784 and 42-29867 flew with the 384th BG on 14 Oct 1943 (384th BG loading lists), and 42-29988 (MACR 914) is not in any 381st record for this date - treated as NOT 381st losses on this mission.

aircraft.loss_details: Hit by fighters (No. 3 engine knocked out) and set on fire after crossing the target, about 1/3 of the way back; six parachutes seen (534th BS diary). Aircraft exploded and crashed at Hausen, about 3 miles east of Schweinfurt (b17flyingfortress.de / AAM). 4 KIA, 6 POW.
aircraft.notes: The only 381st BG aircraft lost on 14 Oct 1943 (381st casualty list, MACR list, 535th BS diary: "losing only one aircraft"). CONFLICTS: squadron 534th per 534th BS diary and 381st MACR list, but 533rd/code VP-P per 381st BGMA aircraft roster; b17flyingfortress.de lists code GD-P (534th) among codes and a photo caption of 533rd. The 534th BS diary gives the aircraft number as "A/C 903" (likely a typo for 803). A family comment on b17flyingfortress.de says it was a borrowed aircraft as the crew's regular B-17 "Smilin' Through" was under repair (unofficial). Block B-17F-70-BO per b17flyingfortress.de serial-range note.

aircraft.notes: 534th BS diary: "Lt. Miller of A/C 832 landed at Bradwell Bay, England. The crew was reported as safe"; listed as abortive. Serial 42-29832 inferred from the diary's last-three-digit aircraft number and the 381st aircraft roster (42-29832, 534th, GD-H) - PROBABLE, not confirmed. Squadron code/letter from roster (general, not date-specific). The 532nd BS diary also says "Lt Miller returned early from France to land on a coastal base in England" - probably the same crew; pilot first name not documented. pilot_rank: diary gives only "Lt."

aircraft.notes: 532nd BS diary: Lt Hutchens took part and "landed at Warmwell, England on his return from the target", returning to Ridgewell on 15 Oct. Hutchens' memoir (381st BGMA, 2011): No. 1 engine lost oil and the prop would not feather near the target; dropped out of formation, dived into cloud, flew home alone over Paris, landed at an RAF field low on fuel; substitute navigator and bombardier flown that day (not named); waist guns broke loose on take-off. Whether bombs were dropped on the target is not stated. Squadron code VE-C from roster (not date-specific). Pilot rank on date not documented (diary: "Lt"; memoir photo caption "Capt. David Hutchens, 1943"). Co-pilot is referred to only as "Tex" in the memoir (real name not given).

research_gaps: 381st.org (381st BG Memorial Association) currently fails TLS / shows a hosting placeholder; all 381st BGMA material was read from Internet Archive snapshots (2002-2012). The 2015-2017 "Unit-History/Data-Sets/Missions" database required login and was not archived.

No loading list, sortie list or formation chart for 381st mission #39 found; the old 381st.org mission database (2000) and mission pages (2002/2008) do not include 14 Oct 1943. The 381st BG group war diary for October 1943 was not archived.

Aircraft serials are known only for 42-29803 (lost), 42-29832 (PROBABLE, Miller abort) and 42-5725 (Hutchens, from his memoir). All other sorties are known only by pilot surname from squadron diaries.
Only the Yorba crew (42-29803) has a full crew manifest. Ball turret gunner conflict (Boylan vs Harkness) unresolved without MACR 1037 itself.
americanairmuseum.com returned HTTP 403; only search-result summaries used.
Paul Bingley & Mike Peters, "Bomb Group" (381st BG history, Casemate) likely contains the sortie list - not accessible online.
Pilot first names and ranks for most diary-listed pilots not established; crew photo captions on 381st.org are not date-specific and were used only as PROBABLE leads in notes.
